hard_gates.gate: G1 database layer (role the app uses)
hard_gates.evidence: db-inspection.txt. erp_app is not a superuser, has no BYPASSRLS and has NOINHERIT. Every table with tenant_id has RLS enabled and forced. On the tenancy tables, company_scope is RESTRICTIVE. With no tenant bound, erp_app sees 0 companies, branches, tenants and access rows. Bound to alnoor, it sees no gulfsteel rows; an UPDATE of B rows changes 0 rows and an INSERT into B is refused by the policy. SET ROLE postgres and ALTER TABLE ... DISABLE RLS are both refused.

biggest_gap.title: The Companies screen gate never models a user who works in no company: rewriting its 'every company' read as `page.items[0]?.everyCompany !== false` offers New to every newly invited administrator, the server refuses it, and every web test stays green
biggest_gap.detail: Round 7's gap (New and Code offered to an administrator of some companies) and round 8's gap (PU, a default-company change for a user who also works elsewhere) are both closed. On the real build, New, Alt+N, ?open=new and the palette are absent for a one-company and a one-branch administrator, and Code is read-only with its reason (walk-limited.log, shots 04 and 05). PU is caught by the new contract test, and PU2 by both the contract test and G2AccountTakeover. The remaining fault is in CompaniesPage.useEveryCompany. It decides 'works in every company' from the first row of GET /api/tenancy/companies?take=1, and it is right only because of `page.items.length > 0 &&`. screens.test.tsx always serves one company row, so it never models a user whose list is empty. The natural rewrite `page.items[0]?.everyCompany !== false` turns an empty list into 'every company'. That state is not exotic: a user created with the Administrator role has no company access until someone grants it, and an administrator of one company can remove someone's last company. Such a user sees New on Companies, fills the form, and is refused on save. That is the same dead-end class as round 7, for the first screen a newly invited finance or admin lead of a UAE group opens. Fix: in screens.test.tsx, add a companies case where the list answers no rows (with every permission): New absent, Alt+N and ?open=new open nothing. Then add U5b to scripts/tenancy-plant-self-test.mjs. Ideally the server should also send everyCompany outside the rows (for example on /tenant or /workplace), so the screen does not infer it from row 0.
biggest_gap.evidence: plants/web-U5b-optional-chain.diff, applied to web/src/modules/tenancy/CompaniesPage.tsx. With it, `npx vitest run` passes 402/402 (plants/web-U5b-full-suite.log), `npm run test:tenancy-plants` reports 24 plants, all caught (plants/web-U5b-tenancy-plant-selftest.log), and src/modules/tenancy alone passes 90/90. Live check: ERP_PROJECT=x ERP_HTTP_PORT=20270 ERP_DB_PORT=20271 ERP_SEED_VOLUME=2000 ./erp up with the plant, then node ui/no-company-admin.mjs http://localhost:20270 <shot>. The script creates an Administrator, whose access reads no companies, and PUTs access {companies:[]}. Result: 'rows 0 | New offered: 1', 'Alt+N opens a new company form: true', and Ctrl+S answers 'Only someone who works in every company of the workspace may create a company...' (plants/U5b-live.log, shot 09). The same script on the unplanted build gives 'New offered: 0', 'Alt+N opens a new company form: false' (plants/U5b-baseline-live.log, shot 10).

other_findings: Plant results this round (plants/summary.txt). Caught: PU (round 8's miss, by the default-company contract test), PU2 (contract test and G2AccountTakeover bulk), PCODE (company code oracle), NOPERM (reviewed permission map), NOPERM2 (the host refuses to start), TSING (G1ProcessState, plus 22 real tenant-B logo leaks in G1HttpIsolation), BRCODE2 (branch write oracle), and U2, U3, U4 (screens.test.tsx). BRCODE alone has no effect, because the kernel's GuardBranchLimits still answers 403. Missed: U5 and U5b (the biggest gap).

Switching company does not scale past six active companies on a fresh device. With 8 active companies the top bar shows no one-click chips until the user has switched once on that device. Switching then takes 2 clicks (switcher, then company), the same as Odoo's 2 clicks, which would be a tie and so a loss. By keyboard it takes Alt+C, typing and Enter. The harness's switch-company run errors in that state (compare-8companies.log, ui/switch-8.log, shots 06 and 08). The server already knows the user's last workplaces, so recent chips could come from there instead of localStorage.

The Arabic keyboard path still saves a branch whose English name is only the company's English name. On the new company I created, the branch saved as code HQ with nameEn 'Critic Walk AR MGDM Manufacturing LLC' and nameAr 'فرع المصفح' (ui/ar-walk.log, shot 03). On the English path, Ctrl+S on the branch line now adds the branch (round 8 finding fixed): 'Critic Walk M0JR Trading LLC - Jebel Ali' with an Arabic name. In Arabic, Alt+N still focuses the English legal name first.

In Arabic at 1400 px, the companies list clips the Arabic legal-name column at its left edge ('…ـ.م.م'; shot 03). The page itself does not overflow (scrollWidth equals clientWidth) in English or Arabic, including with 8 companies.

Ordering: POST /api/tenancy/companies from a one-company administrator with an incomplete body answers 400 validation before the 403 companyNeedsEveryCompany. With a valid body it answers 403. This is not a leak, but the refusal reason only appears after the form is valid.

The platform-operator CLI works: tenant create, suspend, list, activate, and a duplicate code refused (provisioning.log; the one-time password is redacted). After my runs, tenant list shows alnoor with 14 companies, most of them retired FALCON copies left by comparison runs. Companies can still only be deactivated, not deleted.

The Arabic company profile PDF (format=pdf as admin.ar) embeds NotoSansArabic Regular and Bold (company-profile-ar.pdf). Whether a missing Arabic legal name may fall back to English is still open as needs-human #9.
